title: Hoover Dam's Concrete Would Have Taken 125 Years to Cool

scenes.text: Hoover Dam's concrete would have needed one hundred twenty five years to cool.
Engineers estimated that if it was poured as one solid block, it would still be cooling today.
About three and a quarter million cubic yards of concrete went into the dam.
So they buried more than five hundred eighty miles of pipe inside it.
Cold water ran through the pipes and carried the heat away.
Without that pipe, the dam would still be warm.

description:
Engineers estimated that a single continuous pour of Hoover Dam's concrete would take 125 years to cool.
So they embedded more than 582 miles of cooling pipe in the concrete.
What's the biggest engineering project you have seen in person? Comment below.
first_comment: Hoover Dam needed 582 miles of cooling pipe. What building do you think is the biggest engineering feat?
